END-TO-END ON A REAL PAGE, which is what the guard could have broken. RESOLVED, the download response-shape change flagged at the 12:32 stamp is SAFE and needs no client update - verified independently rather than taken on report. src/blocks/shared-ui/view.js:1817 is the ONLY JavaScript caller of POST /media/{id}/download; it awaits inside a try/catch explicitly commented as a best-effort, non-blocking stat increment and DISCARDS the return value, so nothing reads .views or .downloads off that endpoint. The other .views readers in the codebase are unaffected: media-social/view.js:118 reads data.views from the VIEW endpoint, whose payload is unchanged, and shared-ui/view.js:578 reads a stats object. SECURITY RE-CUT VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY, every hole re-tested from the caller's side rather than from the diff. (1) GET /media/{id}/group, the metadata leak: anonymous and a second member at the same role both get 404 mvs_not_found for a private item and for a private item inside a group, with no title, description or owner in the body; the members-scope item is 404 for anonymous and 200 for a signed-in member; the owner sees everything. The per-member filter is the part that matters and it holds - the public gallery containing one private photo returns ONLY the public id to anonymous and to the other member, and both ids to the owner. 404 rather than 403 throughout, so there is no existence oracle. (2) POST /media/{id}/chapters: owner 200, same-role author 403 mvs_pro_forbidden, subscriber 403, anonymous 401 mvs_pro_unauthorized, admin with moderate_mvs_media 200 - and the refused writes left the stored chapters untouched. Note the first attempt at this test used the wrong payload shape and returned 400 for everyone, which proves nothing about authority; the matrix above is from a schema-valid payload. (3) can_read_media() now resolves privacy: with the video flipped private, chapter reads are 200 for the owner and 404 mvs_pro_not_found for the same-role author, the subscriber and anonymous, with no chapter titles in any refused body. (4) MVS_CSS: a paddingUnit and a marginUnit of "px} </style><script>alert(document.domain)</script><style>" both fall back to px, and the generated CSS contains no angle bracket and no 'script' substring; an unknown unit ('parsecs') falls back too and a legal one ('rem') is honoured. (5) Range clamping over HTTP on a 5065-byte file: bytes=0-999999999 and bytes=0- both return 206 with Content-Length 5065 and Content-Range bytes 0-5064/5065; bytes=0-99 returns 100; bytes=5000-999999 clamps to 65; bytes=99999-100000 returns 416 with Content-Range bytes */5065. Content-Length equalled the delivered body in every case, which is the bug. (6) StorageResolver::safe_stored_name(): report.pdf.php, shell.php, evil.phtml, x.php5, a.PHP, t.phar, script.js and page.html all gain .bin; doc.pdf, sheet.xlsx, notes.md and archive.tar.gz are untouched; weird.php.pdf becomes weird.php_.pdf. A file with no extension also gains .bin, which is harmless because the on-disk name is internal.

VIEW-COUNTER DEDUP REFACTOR RE-RUN, the change flagged as riskiest because it touched a counter that already worked. Sequence as one signed-in member against a fresh fixture: view #1 recorded; view #2 inside the window counted:false with views:1; download #1 WITH A PRIOR VIEW ALREADY PRESENT recorded:true - this is the exact case the old code got wrong, because its dedup asked for 'view' rows, so the download was dropped whenever the visitor had merely viewed the item; download #2 counted:false with downloads:1; view #3 still counted:false with views:1, so view dedup was not broken by the refactor; share #1 recorded:true and share #2 recorded:false, the new transient dedup. Database after the sequence: exactly one 'view' row and one 'download' row for that user, and stats views=1 downloads=1 shares=1 - every event counted once and only once. Downloads are disabled site-wide by default (mvs_allow_downloads), so the option was enabled for this test and restored to its original empty value afterwards; without that step the download leg silently returns 403 and the riskiest path goes untested. CONTRACT CHANGE WORTH ANNOUNCING: the deduped download reply now reports 'downloads' where it previously reported 'views'. That is the fix, but it is a response-shape change shipping in a patch, so any client reading .views off the download endpoint will need updating.

NOT EXERCISED THIS ROUND, and therefore not evidenced: the Pro connector export ownership check. The guard itself reads correctly - it compares media_repository->get_author($media_id) against the calling user and allows moderate_mvs_media through, and get_author() was confirmed to return the true owner id for three sampled items - but ConnectorRESTController's routes are NOT REGISTERED on this site (no /mvs-pro/v1/connectors/* appears in the route index, because the controller is only wired when connectors are configured), so no live request could reach it. It needs a site with a connected remote account: a member requesting export of another member's media id must be refused with 'You can only export your own media.' and must not stamp external_source or external_id onto the victim's row. Counted as skipped, not passed.

PRECONDITION TO ADD TO THE RUNBOOK - assert src vs build parity before a walk. Pro blocks register from MVS_PRO_DIR . 'build/blocks/' (includes/Blocks/BlockRegistrar.php:73-80), and build/ is gitignored (wpmediaverse-pro/.gitignore:23). It is refreshed only by an explicit build, so a clean git tree says nothing about what the site actually renders and the walked site can silently lag the source. That is exactly what happened with pro-document-embed: the fix was correct in src/ but build/ still held the pre-fix file, so the row read as a broken fix for a whole round trip. Packaging does run grunt build -> npm run build:blocks, so the zip would have shipped correct code - the risk is QA certifying a build the release does not contain, in either direction. Suggested check at the top of Global preconditions: for each src/blocks/*/render.php compare against build/blocks/<slug>/render.php and STOP if any differ, the same way a failing fixture cleanup is treated as a release blocker.

(4) C.member.video-poster-fallback names PosterService::is_ffmpeg_available(), which does not exist; PosterService has only dir(), stage_bytes() and stage_client_frame(). (5) D.documents-privacy-vocabulary asserts PRIVACY_VALUES is exactly private/members/public - it is now private/space/members/public. The guarded bug is gone: nothing offers 'unlisted', and unlisted or restricted both answer 400 mvs_document_privacy_invalid.
